section_1.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Smoothie Analogy (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of decomposition. Just as a smoothie can be deconstructed into its original ingredients, any complex signal can be broken down into simple sine waves.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 'Berry-Banana-Kale' smoothie being separated back into three distinct piles of fruit.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: Rotating Vectors (0:45-1:30)
section_2.content: Briefly revisit Euler’s Formula (e^ix = cos x + i sin x). Explain how a signal can be visualized as a point rotating around a circle at different frequencies.
section_2.example: An animation of a vector spinning; the 'shadow' cast on the X-axis creates a sine wave.

section_3.title: The Mechanism: The Center of Mass (1:30-3:00)
section_3.content: Explain the Fourier Transform as a tool that 'wraps' a signal around a center point at a specific frequency. If the frequency matches the signal's component, the center of mass shifts away from the origin.
section_3.example: A complex wave of a chirping bird 'wrapped' around a circle. When the rotation speed matches the bird's pitch, the center of mass spikes—revealing the frequency.

section_4.title: Key Concept: Time Domain vs. Frequency Domain (3:00-4:00)
section_4.content: Contrast the Time Domain (where things happen) with the Frequency Domain (what things are made of). Emphasize that the Fourier Transform is the bridge between these two views.
section_4.example: Side-by-side animation: A piano keyboard playing a chord (Time Domain) vs. a bar chart showing the specific notes being played (Frequency Domain).

section_5.title: Application: Real-World Filtering (4:00-5:00)
section_5.content: Demonstrate why this matters. If we can see the frequencies, we can remove the ones we don't want (Noise Cancellation).
section_5.example: A smartphone character filtering out 'background construction noise' from a voice recording by simply erasing the high-frequency spikes in the Frequency Domain.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
